findings.issue: Still open, and correctly disclosed rather than claimed fixed. Re-verified in the current tree: mask.Apply (mask/mask.go:255-275) returns m.Mask's output unchecked (a custom masker that returns its input yields Masked:true with no error, so the residual filter is fed a digest for a cell that was never masked) and has no deferred recover, so a panicking masker still escapes the module that owns the masker contract. Nothing in this fix round touched mask/ — git status shows no modification to mask/mask.go, consistent with mask/ being a separate module outside T-REDFIX's paths. The other four T-REDFIX findings are fixed and covered: internal/verify/redteam_test.go and internal/classify/redteam_test.go carry the netTally/scoreHits and byteaTextSignal cases, internal/textsig/candidates_test.go carries the spelledDigits alphanumeric-group case, and internal/plan/typeliteral_test.go plus fixtures 016/017 cover --allow-type-literal TYPE=REASON on both the plan and verify sides. make check is green end to end (MAKE_CHECK_EXIT:0; lint clean, all packages ok, mask ok). The developer's three concerns check out against the tree: mask/CLAUDE.md:203-209 does record the deliberate 'no runtime output-must-differ guard' decision (enum label, collapsed special_category); the four recover sites they cite exist (internal/core/run.go:1583,1604, internal/core/channel.go:90, internal/load/load.go:782), so T-0181 is defence in depth rather than an open egress; and T-0180's filed goal text does direct the naive fix ('if the output is non-empty and byte-equal to the input or its canonical form, return a refusal'), which would refuse the correct answer on every closed column.
findings.fix: No further work is possible inside this task's paths. Accept the deferral and close T-REDFIX as 14 of 16 fixed, not done. When scheduling, T-0180's brief must carry mask/ in its paths AND override the task's own goal sentence: the corrected statement is THREAT_MODEL.md T12's 2026-09-15 amendment ('It is not a bare equality comparison... the post-condition has to exempt the closed-column and collapsed paths'), not the tracker goal's byte-equality wording, which predates that correction. Either amend T-0180's goal via the tracker tool before scheduling, or have the scheduling brief quote the THREAT_MODEL T12 wording directly, so the implementer does not read the stale sentence first. postmortem: Went well: the reviewer's finding carried its own remedy ('accept the deferral'), and verifying that state rather than restating it turned up a real in-paths defect — the disclosure text understated the fix, in a way that would have mis-briefed the follow-up task. Went badly: nothing in this round; the round was cheap because rounds 1 and 2 had already landed the fourteen fixes and the tracker entries. Change next time: when a task defers work to another module, the deferral note should be checked against that module's own CLAUDE.md before it is written — mask/CLAUDE.md had already argued the opposite of what T-0180's goal now asks for, and nobody reconciled the two at filing time. A red team round should also be scoped with the module under attack in the developer's paths; attacking mask/ with a fixer who cannot edit mask/ guarantees deferrals.
dev_summary: The single remaining medium finding is one the reviewer itself resolves as "no further work is possible inside this task's paths — accept the deferral as stated." I verified that state rather than taking it on trust: mask/ is a separate Go module (mask/go.mod) and is not in my authorized paths, so mask.Apply (mask/mask.go:249-275) cannot be touched here. T-0180 (post-condition) and T-0181 (recover) are open in the tracker, each naming mask/mask.go and recording that mask/ was outside T-REDFIX's paths, and the debt is disclosed in THREAT_MODEL.md at T7 (panic egress) and T12 (passthrough masker). The one in-paths defect I found was in that disclosure: T12's amendment called the post-condition "one comparison", which contradicts mask/CLAUDE.md's recorded decision that a masked enum and a collapsed special_category are meant to be able to return their input. I corrected that sentence so whoever picks up T-0180 does not ship a bare equality guard. T-REDFIX stands at 14 of 16 fixed.
dev_concerns: T-0180's goal text, as filed, directs a naive implementation that would be wrong. It says: 'after m.Mask, if the output is non-empty and byte-equal to the input or its canonical form, return a refusal.' mask/CLAUDE.md, under 'Decisions made during implementation', records the opposite decision deliberately: '`Apply` has no runtime "output must differ from input" guard' — because a masked enum emits a member label and a collapsed special_category emits the first label, so both are *meant* to be able to return the input. A bare equality guard would refuse the correct answer on every closed column, and the fix would either be reverted (leaving the debt) or ship as a plan/load failure on enum columns. Whoever schedules T-0180 needs mask/ in their paths *and* a brief that says the post-condition must exempt the closed-column (labelValue) and collapsed paths. I corrected THREAT_MODEL.md T12's amendment to say this, since that file is in my paths and the tracker goal quotes it; I did not edit the tracker task itself, because writing to an existing task is not the one tracker write (`tracker.py new`) a task authorizes.

T-0181 (recover in mask.Apply) is defence in depth, not an open leak: internal/core/run.go:1583 and :1604, internal/core/channel.go:90 and internal/load/load.go:782 already recover, and core.PanicSummary redacts the recovered value. The residual exposure T-0181 closes is that the module owning the masker contract does not name the masker id and category in the converted error. Worth scheduling, but it is lower severity than T-0180.

T-REDFIX should be closed as 14 of 16, not done. The two open items are the reviewer's finding, and both are outside this task's authorization boundary by module, not by oversight. Scheduling them needs a task whose paths include mask/ — no task in this phase has had that yet, so mask/mask.go has gone through the red team round unmodified.
